title: Lightly Spiced Japanese Pork Gyoza
description: Earthy and creamy Japanese dish featuring puff pastry and ferment kimchi, inspired by Okinawan cuisine, with a touch of ayurvedic rajasic friendly spices.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large bowl, combine the ground pork, chopped kimchi, soy sauce, sesame oil, grated ginger, and minced garlic, and mix well.
Roll out the puff pastry on a floured surface to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Use a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass to cut out circles of pastry.
Place a tablespoon of the pork mixture in the center of each pastry circle.
Brush the edges of the pastry with a little water, then fold the pastry in half to form a half-moon shape, and press the edges together to seal.
Place the gyoza on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving about 1 inch of space between each gyoza.
Brush the tops of the gyoza with a little sesame oil, and sprinkle with chopped green onions.
Bake the gyoza in the preheated oven for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown.
Serve the gyoza hot with your favorite dipping sauce.
